title: Europe’s AI Dreams Exceed Its Grid
content: Europe is racing to expand its AI data-center capacity, but its power grids are already strained, and local communities are increasingly pushing back against new construction. Achieving technological sovereignty will require less grandstanding and more practical solutions that make better use of existing resources.

title: What the US Midterms Could Mean for AI
content: Now that the Democrats will hold sizable majorities in both chambers of the US Congress, they have an opening to push for long-overdue legislation to steer AI development toward the common good. Private companies should not have the power to decide unilaterally which risks the public will bear.

title: Let’s Publish AI-Generated Articles!
content: Peer-reviewed academic journals exist to advance our knowledge and understanding by publishing the best work being done in a given field. If that is the goal, and the best reviewers—both human and AI—agree that an article generated by AI meets that standard, why should a journal's editors reject it?

title: The AI Industry Should Make Something People Want
content: AI companies have alienated Americans by forcing them to bear the costs of their products while treating their consent as optional. With voters across the United States rejecting data centers, the incoming Congress has an opportunity to enact meaningful regulation and hold the industry accountable.

title: It’s the Corruption, Stupid
content: Fed up with Donald Trump and his family's blatant profiteering, Americans dealt Republicans a resounding defeat in this month’s midterm elections. Democrats won by linking corruption to the cost-of-living crisis, but the party’s establishment remains compromised and must clean house before 2028.

title: The Right Lessons From Brazil and the US
content: One lesson progressives in both countries cannot afford to ignore is that recent election results do not amount to a mandate. Neither the Democrats in the US nor President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s Workers' Party in Brazil are offering a vision voters can get excited about.

title: A Russian Bribe the Size of Europe
content: US President Donald Trump is willing to sacrifice Ukraine in exchange for lucrative oil and gas deals with Russia, but this bargain is bound to backfire spectacularly. Vladimir Putin has a long record of betraying his business partners, and once he gets what he wants from Trump, Europe will be his next target.

title: Will Anthropic’s IPO Lead to Better AI Regulation?
content: When frontier AI labs go public, ordinary people’s investments and pensions become tied to their valuations and stock prices. While excessive regulation could undermine a firm’s growth, catastrophic accidents caused by inadequate safety measures could do the same—and wipe out shareholder value.

title: A Minimum Basic Income Is Not Enough
content: The rise of AI is concentrating wealth and political power in fewer and fewer hands, making extreme inequality a threat to democracy itself. A universal basic share that gives ordinary people a portion of global profits could help narrow the growing gap between billionaires and everyone else.

title: Scott Bessent’s Risky Short-Termism
content: The US Treasury secretary's commitment to accelerate buybacks of longer-term debt and issue more short-term debt in their place promises significant budgetary savings. But if borrowing costs rise, what happens in the T-bill market won’t stay in the T-bill market.

title: Why Politicians Love Stimulus Checks
content: Stimulus checks sent to households promise to supercharge the economy, but much of the money simply sits in people's bank accounts. They are popular with voters but do little to address the underlying causes of economic downturns and leave future generations to foot the bill.

title: Who’s Winning (and Who’s Losing) the Ocean? — Marie-May Jeremie
content: Ahead of COP31, PS sat down with Marie-May Jeremie, Minister of Environment, Climate, Energy and Natural Resources of the Republic of Seychelles, to discuss the logic of “blue” economic development. Watch as she describes the deeply personal stakes for small island states, and calls on the global community to support their efforts.

title: The Midterms Won’t Change Much for US Allies
content: Even if the Democrats’ midterm victory marks the beginning of the end of the Trump administration’s “America First” approach to foreign affairs, it does not augur the return of a consistent, reliable US foreign policy. America's friends and allies around the world will have to continue to hedge their bets.

title: Revolts of the Young
content: Young protesters have taken to the streets in France, India, Serbia, and several other countries, rising up against corrupt mainstream parties and economic inequality. But their efforts to improve liberal democracy will likely be overshadowed by the far right’s far more organized efforts to seize power.

title: The Economic Toll of Israel’s Wars
content: Israel’s economy may look strong, but three years of war have inflicted far greater damage than its robust stock market and appreciating currency suggest. Defense spending and government borrowing have risen sharply, while falling output and investment point to a prolonged recession.

content: Prior to the US midterm elections on November 3, financial markets had been treating generative AI as some kind of unstoppable force that could not be hampered by higher interest rates or political and social resistance. But now reality may be setting in.

title: The Mismeasure of Privacy
content: Over the past few decades, we have adopted a new framework for thinking about privacy that centers our experience in the digital realm, conflates privacy with secrecy, and fails to account for the insecurity surveillance generates. As a result, even privacy advocates often undermine their own cause.

title: What the ILO Can Teach a Divided World
content: In a world where compromise is held in contempt, collective action is increasingly difficult. The International Labour Organization’s decades-long record of bringing workers, employers, and governments to the negotiating table has been exceptional in this regard, demonstrating the necessity and potential of multilateralism.

title: The Five Stages of AI Grief
content: Like those diagnosed with a terminal illness, humanity is being forced through the stages of denial, anger, bargaining, depression, and acceptance as AI’s capabilities and potential rapidly expand. But there is a crucial difference: AI and its uses are not outside our control.
